- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and forecast is falling sharply, avoid excessive downward bias — consider mean reversion toward recent highs.  
- If recent price action shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of sharp reversal), adjust forecast to reflect momentum correction.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in 30d horizon) are common — cap forecast peaks at 1.2x recent 7-day high to prevent overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), forecast should align with recent 14-day moving average, not extreme 30d trend.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust subsequent days downward if sentiment remains weak, or upward if sentiment strengthens.  
- Avoid forecasting below 10% of recent 30-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish and confirmed by 2+ consecutive negative sentiment readings.
